notes.title: Way of Rhea releases TOMORROW!
notes.content:
Way of Rhea is releasing [b]TOMORROW[/b]!

This blog series walks through some of the mechanics featured in the game. Be warned: mild spoilers ahead! This post covers The End Game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/1bc5435577171f7f5197da0241ac4da9251b702d.gif[/img]

For many players, the biomes up until this point will be sufficiently challenging, and some players may be happy to solve most of those puzzles and stop.

However for avid puzzlers, everything we've seen so far is just set up for the real challenge: the end game.

The end game combines everything we've learned so far into 4 levels of very challenging puzzles.

[h2]Snow Crab + Circuits[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/018e080b74b733e6bba30c97ad7f1e376f64c115.gif[/img]

This area combines Snow Crab style puzzles with circuit puzzles. It's the easiest of the end game levels.

[h2]Staves + Circuits[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/f0fb720fbc36868c1e4298af43708bdf97f4f332.gif[/img]

The next area combines staves and circuits. Since both staves and circuits are very stateful, these can get very tricky.

[h2]Snow Crab + Staves[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/d7c969d0ea20367cb917b971a72fd4266c7c5a3c.gif[/img]

The penultimate level combines Snow Crab style puzzles with staff puzzles. The Snow Crab will now interact with staves just as he would any other object, and you can take staves from him just as you could take an orb from him, resulting in him being colorless.

[h2]Snow Crab + Staves + Circuits[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/f0fb720fbc36868c1e4298af43708bdf97f4f332.gif[/img]

The final level combines *all* of the above mechanics, for a final challenge requiring mastery over everything in the game.

[h2]Other Features[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/d4258bdc5911df93c77da43fa1f42166ed823ec0.jpg[/img]

Once you've beat all the puzzles, you can use the speedrunning features to try to improve your time. There are also some achievements to collect.

[h2]And that's it![/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/dc654b1f988b715fd9d025179dfb8d6930823d51.gif[/img]

...or is it?

Don't forget to wishlist Way of Rhea on Steam, I can't wait to get it in people's hands tomorrow. :)

Cheers,
Mason

notes.title: Way of Rhea releases in 2 days!
notes.content:
Way of Rhea is releasing in [b]2 days![/b]

This blog series walks through some of the mechanics featured in the game. Be warned: mild spoilers ahead! This post covers The Professor's Biome.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/4896e9ec63694470574d5a17c6063056eed24c18.gif[/img]

[i]The professor is kind of a jerk.[/i]

This area introduces The Professor, and a new way to change colors using staves.

[h2]Staves[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/8be5ec01fbcb8004cae56dfa084a3be3e6439e14.gif[/img]

Normally, to change color, you'd need an orb and a lamp.

In this biome you can *instantly* change color by dropping your staff, and picking up a staff that's a different color. Unlike orbs, staves are infinitely reusable, so you can switch back and forth as much as you like--provided you're able to return to where you left the original staff!

[h2]Colorless[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/936feb2ee19e40266b7a048006f8a734c5bc3a0a.gif[/img]

You can also drop your staff without picking up a new one, and as a result have no color. This couldn't possibly be useful...or could it?

[h2]With great power...[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/ad5ccdf20fbbd38a5316e533205a14b1388bc53b.gif[/img]

Staves are, in a sense, more powerful than orbs:

[olist]
[*] They can be reused
[*] You can change color at any location you're able to get a staff to, not just at lamps
[/olist]

As a result of all this power, puzzles have a lot more possible solutions to explore--but typically still only one solution that works, making these puzzles a bit more difficult.

Don't forget to wishlist Way of Rhea on Steam! I'll see you tomorrow in *The End Game*, where the real challenge begins...

Cheers,
Mason

notes.title: Way of Rhea releases in 3 days!
notes.content:
Way of Rhea is releasing in 3 days!

This blog series walks through some of the mechanics featured in the game. Be warned: mild spoilers ahead! This post covers Rhea's Biome.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/5f00955d80bb788191a1cfb5bca09dfd325feaf2.gif[/img]

This area introduces Rhea, and color circuits.

[h2]Color Circuits[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/cfff09c42a89aadd1872e21e4a877df54093fff6.gif[/img]

Circuits introduce a new way to open gates.

Normally, you need to be the same color as a gate to open it. However, if a gate has a circuit attached to it, you can alternatively place an orb of matching color onto the circuit to open the gate.

This will not change your color, and you can retrieve the orb later (if you don't mind the gate re-closing.)

[h2]Multi Gate Circuits[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/a8daae4ef6ebf3d4405c92d2cdc05f9f09a8b8a9.gif[/img]

If a circuit has multiple gates on it, color flows through the circuit from the place the orb was placed. Only gates of matching color will open.

[h2]Color Conflicts[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/7c16951b02514d5a59afd6fb38f796b263f55238.gif[/img]

Color flows through the circuit segment by segment from each placed orb simultaneously.

If multiple orbs of differing colors are placed on a circuit, the color stops flowing at the point at which the non matching colors meet. This can prevent you from progressing, but it can also be used to your advantage.

[h2]Progression[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/221858a0e69bceb125f188d824f403f6d3e80786.gif[/img]

These puzzles are not as difficult as the end game puzzles, but they start to get more difficult than most of what we saw in the intro.

Don't forge to wishlist Way of Rhea! I'll see you tomorrow in The Professor's Biome...

Cheers,
Mason

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/a058b009f4bcab283ec0c98d91e2a7ef1b41f871.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/c10dc67bbc3bb920758fa9c0b0e6cb59c2916b3f.gif[/img]

notes.title: Way of Rhea releases in 5 days!
notes.content:
Way of Rhea releasing in 5 days!

This blog series walks through some of the mechanics featured in the game. Be warned: mild spoilers ahead! This post covers the second area in the game, Snow Crab's Biome.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/67430265137f9189ce54b4edf578cd11e81a3b08.gif[/img]
[i]Hermie got lost in the Ice Caves trying to help his dad, you need to save him![/i]

This area introduces Snow Crab, and how you can use his behavior patterns to solve puzzles.

[h2]Working With Snow Crab[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/c6d4c2811c2c56b81ee1605099a26209fb3c43aa.gif[/img]

Snow Crab will walk until he hits an obstacle, and then turn around. Repeat. Along the way, if he finds any interactive items--orbs, lamps, elevators, teleporters, etc--he will interact with them.

Additionally, he can cross paths covered by ice crystals and you cannot.

While he's not clever enough to follow instructions, you can toss him objects, or take objects back from him by interacting with them, using his motion to your advantage.

As always, undo/redo is available if you make a mistake.

[h2]Time Controls[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/db03e5221e1f6ba57e60cfc5d5b0c67ee675b80f.gif[/img]

To avoid requiring overly precise real time control--and to avoid requiring waiting--you can pause or fastforward time whenever you want, which is especially useful when working with Snow Crab.

[h2]Teleporters[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/61baa823ebd18b8229741b46cb69ba44ccec875f.gif[/img]

Snow Crab will interact with any objects that cross his path--including teleporters. If a teleporter is enabled, he'll turn it off. If it's not, he'll set it as his destination.

A teleporter only has one user at a time. This means that you'll need to coordinate teleporter use with Snow Crab.

[h2]Progression[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/678a7c69fb02f052cc93c42249338f01b5956e31.gif[/img]

We're still in the introductory area of the game, but this biome has a couple  of puzzles near the end that are quite difficult. The interaction between you, Snow Crab, and the teleporters has a lot of interesting edge cases for puzzles to exploit, the state space starts to blow up here.

Don't forget to wishlist Way of Rhea! I'll see you tomorrow in The Overworld...

Cheers,
Mason

notes.title: Way of Rhea releases in 6 days!
notes.content:
In celebration of Way of Rhea releasing on Steam in 6 days, I'm making a post a day about a different aspect of the game.

Let's look at the first area of the game: Shrew's Biome.

Be warned--this blog series features mild spoilers!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/e495d52d374647119b540e925311a2f22164c88a.gif[/img]

[i]Shrew is your excitable friend who's very invested in you solving the forest puzzles tonight for some reason.[/i]

[h2]Color Changing[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/6ba9bfe1b06bf34b848cfc0a972fe1a0c992f6e9.gif[/img]

[i]From left to right: gate, lamp, orb, & you.[/i]

Way of Rhea's main mechanic is the ability to change colors. You can enter gates and elevators when you match their color, otherwise you cannot.

To change color, you place a colored orb into a lamp. Upon doing this, you become the color of the orb and the orb is destroyed.

[h2]Teleportation[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/cf42a3f5d0b11afe3eddf06934eff312826e547a.gif[/img]

Teleportation in Way of Rhea requires two steps:
[olist]
[*] Set a teleporter as your destination by interacting with it
[*] Interact with any other teleporter in the map to be sent back to this destination
[/olist]
As a result, you can only teleport to locations that you've already been.

[h2]Undo/Redo[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/6448be2e35e3ddfdc9d22f9a6e593128e9bfa5db.gif[/img]

This clip also shows off the undo/redo mechanic that is taught in this biome. As you progress through the game the puzzles become difficult to solve, but you're always free to explore different options without committing to them through use of undo/redo.

[h2]Orb/Tele Fields[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/df17a72f9aa924f4b7b21246dd78cbb259ed1a92.gif[/img]

As the puzzles increase in difficulty, orb and tele fields are introduced. Orb fields (right) prevent you from carrying orbs across them, whereas tele fields (left) disable the active teleport destination when they are crossed.

[h2]Difficulty[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/6d749abcaa028d23f12b1ef033e7bfe88140f5ce.gif[/img]

As you progress through the biome, the puzzles increase in difficulty as you're increasingly required to take advantage of edge cases of the mechanics to progress. That being said, this is still the intro area, and seasoned puzzle gamers likely won't have much trouble with it.

I'll see you tomorrow in Snow Crabs's Biome...

Cheers,
Mason

notes.title: The Ice Biome
notes.content:
While the focus of Way of Rhea will always be on the puzzles, visuals are important. Visuals are what build the world, they dictate entire vibe of the game. Without them the game loses its context, and the pieces of the puzzles lose their meaning. If you've played past demos, you've seen that most of the levels lack environmental art—we always block puzzles out before committing to them. This is also why the Steam trailer only shows off the first level!

This past month, we've started work on a new process for getting art into the game that lets us add art to the puzzles before they "go gold". We no longer have to wait until we're certain we won't tweak a puzzle to get its visuals in place.

Using this new process, we started adding artwork to the [i]Ice Biome[/i]. These visuals aren't final yet, but they're close, so I wanted to share them with you!

notes.title: Festival Demo Update: Your Feedback!
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

Thanks for checking out the Way of Rhea demo, and for all the feedback! :) I took some time today to make some adjustments to the demo in response to your suggestions.

As a side note—most of the feedback I received was via social media ([url=https://twitter.com/anthropicst]@anthropicst[/url]), or email (anthropicstudios+support@gmail.com). Those are both great ways to get in touch, but we also check the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1110620/discussions/]community hub[/url]—it just looks a little dead right now since all previous demos were private or at in person festivals. :)

Onto the changes...

[h2]The Music[/h2]

A number of people told me that they found the tempo changes in levels 00 and 03 distracting. In hindsight this makes sense—I was using our trailer music in game, it was written to really quickly build in intensity, not to comfortably loop in the background.

I ran this by one of our composers, and he already had a few tracks queued up. I went ahead and swapped in two of those, so the demo now has some new, less distracting music!


[h2]Undo/Redo[/h2]

In Way of Rhea, you can undo any action of consequence. However, the game doesn't yet do a good job teaching you to use this mechanic, so some of you understandably thought you were softlocked when you ran out of orbs!

Longer term I'm planning on building a puzzle early on that teaches you how to undo, for now I just threw up a giant banner on game start mentioning that "Q" is undo to make things clearer. :)

[h2]Accessibility[/h2]

A couple of folks mentioned having trouble differentiating between the orb colors. Long term we're planning on modifying the artwork to differ in silhouette as well as color, but for now I figured it was worth building in a short term solution.

If you press escape and check out the options menu, there's a setting called "high contrast colors". If you enable this, the interactive items in the game will switch to a colorblind friendly palette. Note that the options menu does not currently persist through restarts, though it will in the final game.


Thanks again for playing, enjoy the rest of the festival! :)

Cheers,
Mason

notes.title: Way of Rhea Demo @ The Steam Game Festival!
notes.content:
Way of Rhea is a puzzle platformer in which you can only interact with objects in the world that match your current color. Rules aren't taught explicitly, you must discover them on your own.

The game is focused on puzzle solving rather than execution skill—you can't die, and all actions with consequences can be undone, so you're free to explore the full possibility space of the puzzle while searching for a solution.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/767fbaac8e480707bd1bc87a06082c7417630bed.gif[/img]

[h2]What's Included?[/h2]

As part of the Steam Game Festival, we're releasing a free demo of the game that should go live on the store page at 10am PDT June 16th. Way of Rhea is still a work in progress, launch is about a year away, but we wanted to build a demo that felt worthwhile! It should be a quick download (shy of 50mb) and includes the following:

[h3]Vertical Slice[/h3]

The first level of the game, with full artwork, is included in the demo. It's short, likely 3-10 minutes depending on your familiarity with puzzle games, but is a good intro to the game.

[h3]Extra Levels[/h3]

After beating the first level, you'll have the option to try three additional levels by selecting the [i]Extra Levels[/i] menu. These levels are still a work in progress and as such don't have full artwork or any narrative, but we wanted to give you some more content to try out so you can see where we're planning on taking the game. We haven't timed people playing these levels, but we expect that they're 25-35 minutes worth of gameplay. If you're a really experienced puzzle solver it's definitely possible to solve them faster.

[h2]Accessibility & Supported Platforms[/h2]

While the game itself is listed as running on macOS and Windows, the festival demo only supports Windows.

[strike]Additionally, the final game will either have a color blind mode, or use icons to make a separate mode unnecessary. Unfortunately this is not yet built into the game.[/strike]

There's now a high contrast color mode available in the settings menu! The plan to add icons and/or change the silhouettes in the long term hasn't changed, but we plan to keep this option around as well.

[h2]Support[/h2]

We're a small team—I'm the only programmer! I've done my best to make sure the demo runs smoothly everywhere, but if I missed anything definitely let me know either on the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1110620/discussions/]Steam discussion page[/url] or via email at [i]anthropicstudios+support@gmail.com[/i]!

Cheers,
Mason

notes.title: Artists' Alley #1: Abstract Palettes and Environment
notes.content:
[b]DISCLAIMER: This is a repost of a very old post Carrie made on [url=https://www.anthropicstudios.com/blog/]our blog[/url] prior to when we had a Steam page. Future posts will be mirrored here immediately. :)[/b]

Artists Alley is a segment which provides a behind the scenes glance into the artistic process for Way of Rhea (WoR).

This segment is essentially a journal that helps me keep organized and focused. Additionally, I hope these updates will provide insight to other newbie gaming artists, game developers who are working with artists, and curious individuals.

That said, I am beyond excited about this project! And I hope you all will join me on this journey full of magic, whimsy, and learning <];{D>

---

So far, I am happy about the existing color palette for [WoR]. I have been exploring how this palette can be manipulated to create different environments and moods. This can be done by changing weight on different colors within the palette. 

For instance, when pale pink is the most prominent color, the world becomes a bit bubble-gummy and light.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/4a89d73b3c0d0b4cdeba2665f66444dd5b5cbff0.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/d80eaf4732360fcb0031f42aa6e944c4ad588b2f.jpg[/img]

While oranges, and deep purple dominating the scene brings to mind more mysterious deep feelings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/b3531e400a6c46d012993640cc8a3ce76cccce03.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/876e9ae0a9b55004da7dd681856d0b8511c1892a.jpg[/img]

Aesthetics I want to achieve, when I get a better feel for setting include:
A sense of curiosity, mystery, a pinch of fun, and a color scheme that can be variable for different moods. 

As the game progresses and the plot unfolds, the background will reflect intended emotions. 
Some levels will be a bit darker, and should feel a bit scary. While other levels should be light and whimsical. In addition to color, terrain make up is important for game design. Different terrains can lead to different obstacles (water, vines, gaps, etc...)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/6856f991e8eac5ad5ce39b9db28e5f99c4a27450.jpg[/img]
 
Another factor to explore through environment is physics. What is the gravity of the environment? Are there any special ‘rules’? [WoR] is a puzzle game. So if for instance, the terrain is mirrored, the character you are controlling can have a reflection plane which mimics the players moves. To make things interesting, there could be some ‘inconsistencies’ between these planes, and the player can switch planes to solve puzzles and overcome obstacles.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/ca24929fbe1c259b5b387ea65a30c473301d27be.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35599024/ceb06a334ef3f4c6465056f3515103077267e9ad.jpg[/img]

Carrie @ Anthropic
